values.meaning: bonus magic damage on critical strikes
values.binNote: Bin models this as a 10% + 0.1%-per-AP amplification of the critical strike's pre-mitigation damage, not a flat percent damage value; wiki phrasing '10% (+10% per 100 AP) bonus magic damage' matches 0.1 + 0.001xap as a multiplier on crit damage.

mechanics.claim: The bonus damage is calculated based on the total damage of the critical strike, before mitigation.
mechanics.quote: The '''bonus''' damage is calculated based on the total damage of the critical strike {{tt|pre-mitigation|Damage calculated before modifiers}}.

mechanics.claim: The bonus damage applies life steal.
mechanics.quote: The '''bonus''' damage {{tip|applies life steal|applies}} {{sti|{{as|life steal}}}}.

mechanics.claim: If the critical strike is already magic damage, the passive amps it directly; otherwise it deals the bonus as a separate new instance of magic damage tagged as a critical strike.
mechanics.quote: If the ''critical strike'' is {{as|magic damage}} then ''Vow of the First Lands'' amps it directly. Otherwise, it deals it as a new instance of {{as|'''bonus''' magic damage}} tagged as having ''critically struck''.

mechanics.claim: When dealt as a new instance, that instance can itself critically strike again, causing the passive to apply again as an amp on itself.
mechanics.quote: When dealt as a new instance, it can ''critically strike'' again (e.g {{ii|Shadowflame}}), successivelly causing ''Vow of the First Lands'' to apply again on itself as an amp.

values.quote: expire one by one every {{fd|0.5}} seconds after the duration

mechanics.claim: Cultivation of Spirit's active attack resets Yunara's basic attack timer.
mechanics.quote: Cultivation of Spirit {{tip|basic attack reset|resets}} '''Yunara's''' basic attack timer.

mechanics.claim: The active gives a 40% lower attack windup and an uncancellable windup, in addition to increased missile speed.
mechanics.quote: augmenting her basic attacks to have increased missile speed, a 40% lower {{tip|attack windup|windup}} time, and an {{tip|uncancellable windup}}

mechanics.claim: Spread attacks apply life steal and on-hit effects and can critically strike if the triggering attack does.
mechanics.quote: Each spread attack {{tip|applies lifesteal|applies}} {{as|{{sti|life steal}}}} and {{tip|on-hit}} effects, with on-hit damage reduced to 30% effectiveness, and will {{tip|critically strike}} if the triggering attack does.

mechanics.claim: The passive/active on-hit damage will critically strike for 0% bonus damage when the triggering attack does, so it is not increased by crit but is reduced by Randuin's Omen.
mechanics.quote: The ''on-hit'' will {{tip|critical strike|critically strike}} for 0% '''bonus''' damage when the triggering attack does

mechanics.claim: There is no limit to the number of enemies the empowered attacks can spread to.
mechanics.quote: There is no limit to the number of enemies the empowered attacks can spread to.

mechanics.claim: While inactive, basic attacks generate a stack of Unleash which refreshes on subsequent attacks; the ability has no cooldown but a minimum downtime determined by attack speed and stack generation.
mechanics.quote: While ''Cultivation of Spirit'' has no cooldown, the ability has a minimum downtime that is the time it takes for '''Yunara''' to generate 8 stacks.

W.name: Arc of Judgment / Arc of Ruin

castTime.quote: {{pp|0.45 to 0.225 for 11|0 to 100|key1=%|type='''bonus''' attack speed|label1= Bonus AS|color=attack speed|round=3}}
castTime.binNote: Base cast time is 0.45s (YunaraW.Cast_Time_Base), reduced toward a minimum of 0.225s (Cast_Time_Min) as bonus attack speed approaches the 100% cap (Cast_Time_Attack_Speed_Cap); this scaling with attacker's own bonus AS is not a per-rank value so only the base is recorded here.

values.binNote: Bin defines Calc_Damage_Per_Second = Calc_Damage_Initial * DPS_Modifier(0.6), i.e. the total damage dealt per second of lingering (4 ticks at the wiki's stated 0.25s interval). Per-tick value = that per-second figure / 4; the 0.25s tick interval itself is not an explicit bin data value, only stated in the wiki description.
Sum of the 4 lingering ticks over the 1s linger equals the per-second value Calc_Damage_Initial * DPS_Modifier(0.6) directly, since 4 ticks x (per-tick=per-second/4) = per-second.

values.quote: lingering as it travels and resetting its remaining duration; upon reaching maximum range, it will expand and linger in place for 1 second

values.binNote: No explicit bin data value for the tick interval; it only appears in the wiki description text and is implied by the DPS_Modifier/4 math in the leveling table.

mechanics.claim: Applies area damage for the initial hit and persistent area damage for the lingering effect.
mechanics.quote: Applies {{tip|area damage}} for the initial hit and {{tip|persistent area damage}} for the lingering effect.

mechanics.claim: The bead can hit the same enemy multiple times with the initial damage if it collides with it again while in flight, and can also deal the lingering effect's damage multiple times (both before and after expansion).
mechanics.quote: ''Arc of Judgment'' can hit an enemy more than once with the initial damage as well with the lingering effect (both while not expanded and while expanded).

mechanics.claim: A spell shield can block either the entire initial hit or a single damage tick of the lingering effect, not both.
mechanics.quote: {{tip|Spell shield}} can block either the initial hit or one damage tick of the lingering effect.

mechanics.claim: Upon reaching maximum range without hitting anything further, the bead expands and lingers in place for 1 second regardless of prior hits.
mechanics.quote: upon reaching maximum range, it will expand and linger in place for 1 second regardless of enemies hit

mechanics.claim: During Transcend One's Self (ultimate), Arc of Judgment is replaced by the upgraded Arc of Ruin, whose damage is treated as ultimate damage for effects like Malignance/Axiom Arcanist, but does not trigger on-ultimate-cast effects.
mechanics.quote: The damage of ''Arc of Ruin'' is considered ultimate damage for the purposes of {{Iis|Malignance}} {{nie|Hatefog}} and {{ri|Axiom Arcanist}}.

values.meaning: Increased Bonus Move Speed (facing enemy champion)

mechanics.quote: ''Untouchable Shadow {{tip|basic attack reset|resets}} '''Yunara's''' basic attack timer. {{ai|Arc of Ruin|Yunara}} can be cast during the dash.

mechanics.claim: Untouchable Shadow does not trigger ultimate cast effects like Zeke's Convergence or Experimental Hexplate.
mechanics.quote: ''Untouchable Shadow'' does not trigger ultimate ''cast'' effects, such as {{iis|Experimental Hexplate}} {{nie|Overdrive}}, {{iis|Zeke's Convergence}} {{nie|Frostfire Tempest}} and {{bi|Cloud Dragon Soul|possessive=true}} increased movement speed.

values.quote: has its {{sti|'''remaining''' cooldown}} reduced by 80% upon both entering and exiting the state

mechanics.claim: During Transcendent State, Cultivation of Spirit automatically activates at no cost, with its duration extended to Transcendent State's duration.
mechanics.quote: Automatically becomes active at no cost, with the duration increased to ''Transcendent State's''.

mechanics.claim: Casting Transcend One's Self also casts Cultivation of Spirit, granting an attack reset if it was not already active.
mechanics.quote: {{ai|Cultivation of Spirit|Yunara}} is cast alongside ''Transcend One's Self''. If the former was not already active, this will also grant its {{tip|basic attack reset|attack reset}}.

mechanics.claim: The attack reset from casting Cultivation of Spirit is not attributed to Transcend One's Self itself, e.g. for the purposes of Hail of Blades.
mechanics.quote: The attack reset does '''not''' originate from ''Transcend One's Self'' nor is ''Transcend One's Self'' tagged as granting one itself (e.g. for the purposes of {{ri|Hail of Blades}}).

mechanics.claim: During Transcendent State, Arc of Judgment is upgraded into Arc of Ruin, which costs no mana.
mechanics.quote: Upgraded into ''{{ai|Arc of Ruin|Yunara}}'', which has no cost and has its {{sti|'''remaining''' cooldown}} reduced by 80% upon both entering and exiting the state.

mechanics.claim: During Transcendent State, Kanmei's Steps is upgraded into Untouchable Shadow, which costs no mana and has its cooldown reset upon both entering and exiting the state.
mechanics.quote: Upgraded into ''{{ai|Untouchable Shadow|Yunara}}'', which has no cost and has its {{sti|cooldown}} reset upon both entering and exiting the state.

mechanics.claim: An ongoing Kanmei's Steps effect is not lost when quickly replaced by Untouchable Shadow.
mechanics.quote: An ongoing ''{{ais|Kanmei's Steps|Yunara}}'' effect is not lost when quickly replaced by ''{{ai|Untouchable Shadow|Yunara}}''.

mechanics.claim: Transcend One's Self cannot be recast while its Transcendent State is already active.
mechanics.quote: ''Transcend One's Self'' cannot be cast again while active.

primitives.note: Critical strikes deal bonus magic damage (Vow of the First Lands); if the crit itself was not magic damage this bonus is dealt as a new tagged 'critical strike' instance that can itself crit and re-trigger the passive as a further amp
Vow's bonus magic damage on every crit; Cultivation of Spirit's passive/active bonus magic damage on every basic attack
Unleash stacks (0-8, +2 per attack on champions/dummy) build from attacking, decay one-by-one every 0.5s after a 6s duration, and gate the active cast (8 stacks + mana required)
Active Unleash grants bonus attack speed and augmented windup for 5s (or Transcendent State's duration when auto-activated by R)
Casting Cultivation of Spirit's active resets the attack timer; Untouchable Shadow's dash (E upgraded by R) also resets the attack timer
Arc of Judgment / Arc of Ruin deals its initial magic damage on impact after a cast time
The bead lingers and deals magic damage every 0.25s for up to 1s (or longer if it keeps colliding, see unsettled)
One W cast produces two separately-timed damage instances: the initial hit and the lingering ticks
Mana (and Q's Unleash stacks) limit how often Q/W/E/R can be cast before Transcendent State removes W's and E's costs and Q's active becomes free
Entering and exiting Transcendent State cuts W's remaining cooldown by 80% (each time) and resets E's cooldown
Transcendent State upgrades W into Arc of Ruin and E into Untouchable Shadow, and auto-activates Q's active for free with extended duration

needsBespoke.why: Vow of the First Lands is self-referential: a crit's bonus magic damage, when dealt as a new tagged 'critical strike' instance, can itself roll a crit and re-trigger the same passive as a multiplicative amp on itself, an iterative/recursive resolution not captured by picking a single crit-interaction primitive. Separately, Cultivation of Spirit's on-hit damage explicitly does NOT get amplified by crit (0% bonus) even though it is tagged as having critically struck for other purposes (e.g. Randuin's Omen), which requires custom sequencing between the onhit-rider and crit-interaction primitives rather than a generic composition of the two.

unsettled.question: What does the unresolved bin calculation YunaraW#{669adf33} (multiplying Calc_Damage_Initial by an unresolved {f3cbe7b2}) actually compute for the lingering tick damage, and does it match the wiki's stated per-tick value of (Initial * 0.6)/4?
options: The bin's unresolved factor equals DPS_Modifier (0.6) applied once per second, split into 4 ticks, matching the wiki figure used here
The unresolved factor differs (e.g. per-tick rather than per-second, or includes another multiplier), making the recorded per-tick/total-expanded damage wrong

unsettled.question: Against a single stationary dummy that the bead keeps colliding with, does the bead's lingering duration keep resetting indefinitely (extending total tick count well past 4), or does it only ever tick up to the stated 1-second linger window regardless of continued collision?
options: Each re-collision resets the linger timer, so continuous contact with a stationary target produces far more than 4 ticks over the fight

The lingering effect is capped/only meaningfully occurs once per cast (expansion at max range or a single linger episode), giving the wiki's stated 4 ticks (~1s) per cast regardless of a stationary target
quotes: The bead slows down significantly while colliding with an enemy, lingering as it travels and resetting its remaining duration; upon reaching maximum range, it will expand and linger in place for 1 second regardless of enemies hit.
''Arc of Judgment'' can hit an enemy more than once with the initial damage as well with the lingering effect (both while not expanded and while expanded).

unsettled.question: How many times, if any, does Vow of the First Lands' recursive self-amp chain resolve per triggering crit in current (non-bugged, intended) behavior — is it meant to potentially recurse indefinitely on repeated crit rolls, or is there an intended cap (e.g. one extra application) that the bug tags suggest isn't yet enforced?
options: Recursion is unbounded by design, continuing as long as each new instance itself crits
Recursion is capped at one extra application, and further recursion is a bug (per the {{bug|2}} tags) not intended to be modeled as unlimited
quotes: When dealt as a new instance, it can ''critically strike'' again (e.g {{ii|Shadowflame}}), successivelly causing ''Vow of the First Lands'' to apply again on itself as an amp. {{bug|2}}

unsettled.question: During Transcendent State, once Cultivation of Spirit auto-activates for free, does it ever need to be manually recast or does it simply persist (matching R's remaining duration) with no further stack/mana cost until R ends?
options: It auto-activates once and persists for the rest of Transcendent State with zero further cost or recast needed
It could still expire/need recasting within the 15s window under some condition not stated in the sources
quotes: {{lc|{{ai|Cultivation of Spirit|Yunara}}}} Automatically becomes active at no cost, with the duration increased to ''Transcendent State's''.

proposal: At the start of the 15s fight, immediately cast R (Transcend One's Self): this has no cast time, auto-activates Cultivation of Spirit (Q) for free with its duration extended to match R's 15s, upgrades W into the free, cheaper-cooldown Arc of Ruin, and upgrades E into Untouchable Shadow.

For the rest of the fight, basic-attack continuously as the core damage source, benefiting from Q's bonus attack speed, Q's passive+active on-hit magic damage, and P's (Vow of the First Lands) bonus magic damage on every crit.
Cast Arc of Ruin (W) on cooldown throughout the fight (free cost, cooldown cut 80% on entering the state) for its initial hit plus lingering tick damage.

Cast Untouchable Shadow (E) on cooldown purely for its attack-reset effect (and to re-enable an immediate Arc of Ruin cast during the dash), timed just before an auto-attack would otherwise land so it effectively grants an extra attack.
Do not recast R again during the fight (15s cooldown at rank 1 already exceeds the fight length, and it cannot be recast while its Transcendent State is active anyway).
questions: Does R's 15s Transcendent State duration match/cover the entire simulated 15s damage fight exactly, or is there any startup delay before its effects (Q auto-activation, W/E upgrades) apply?

In a fixed-position dummy fight, should Untouchable Shadow's dash be modeled as simply granting an attack reset with no positional benefit (since there's nowhere useful to dash), or does the simulator need to account for its dash distance/cast requirements at all?
Should Arc of Ruin be cast as soon as it comes off (reduced) cooldown, or held to line up with Untouchable Shadow's attack-reset window for maximum total attacks landed?

Is entering Transcendent State immediately at t=0 actually optimal, or would delaying R slightly (to first build Unleash stacks / land a manual Cultivation of Spirit cast) produce more total damage over the fixed 15s window?
